sample.source: Where you found these postings: job sites, company job boards, a recruiter.
searches: Each search exactly as you typed it, with its location filter.
sample.inclusion: The role's core work is building or running shared AI or agent infrastructure, tooling, guardrails or platforms that other teams, products or agents use. A title alone does not qualify.
sample.exclusion: Forward-deployed and solutions or sales roles, AI trainer and data annotation gigs, general software roles whose AI content is incidental, management and delivery-director roles.
sample.limits: What your sample cannot tell you: dates, places, search terms you chose, sites you could not read.

codebook.type: Primary kind of job: infrastructure (running, serving or training AI at scale), enablement (shared AI capabilities, standards and governance for many internal teams), product-agents (agents or LLM features inside a customer-facing product), coding-agents (coding agents and AI developer tooling in engineering workflows), applied (a domain-specific AI system). alsoType records a clear second kind.
codebook.agents: Builds, runs or governs AI agents (a model calling tools in a loop) or agentic workflows.
codebook.codingAgents: Names or clearly describes AI coding agents or assistants as something the role builds for, operates or requires.
codebook.retrieval: Retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, embeddings or document-processing pipelines.
codebook.evaluation: Evaluating model or AI output: golden sets, eval harnesses, model judges, quality gates, evaluation pipelines.
codebook.guardrails: Guardrails, governance, policy, permission scoping for AI, or architectural constraints on AI output.
codebook.aiObservability: Monitoring, logging, tracing or metrics for AI or ML systems.
codebook.costControl: Token cost, spend limits, cost attribution, or compute cost optimization for AI.
codebook.humanApproval: Human review queues, approvals, or human-in-the-loop for AI actions.
codebook.security: Security or compliance named as a responsibility or requirement.
codebook.servingOrTraining: Model serving or inference infrastructure, training, fine-tuning or GPU capacity, as required or preferred.
codebook.languages: Named as required or preferred. typescriptOrJavascript includes Node.js and React.
codebook.gateway: An LLM gateway that centralizes model access, keys, limits and cost, or routing between models by cost and capability.
codebook.gatewayBasis: Optional: where a posting's gateway code came from, when you add the signal after the posting was first coded. text (its full text when first read), reread (its full text read again later), note (its note, when the text can no longer be reached).
codebook.readOn: The day you read the posting in full and coded it, as YYYY-MM-DD. The template's date is a placeholder: replace it.
codebook.publicWorkAsked: Postings with "architect" in the title only: whether the posting asks, in so many words, for a public body of work (a public repository, published writing or talks, a governance framework or an architecture decision record). required (an application must include it), asked (the application asks for a link), preferred (desired, a plus, or one accepted form of evidence), none, or not re-read (the text could not be reached to check).
codebook.screenedOn: On exclusion records: the day you screened the posting out, as YYYY-MM-DD.

postings.title: Replace with the title as posted
postings.source: Replace with where you found it
postings.note: One sentence on the core work, in your own words. Say why you coded any borderline field the way you did.

excluded.title: A posting you read and left out
